text:
jana: FYI I hit a reproducible drift when we load a roundtripped int4 checkpoint for very long prefixes (~70k tokens). Shorter prefixes look fine. Minimal repro and notes below.

omar: paste the exact repro command?

jana:```bash
# runs on cpu and nvgpu to rule out device-specific aliasing
python -m tests.longctx_compare \
  --model checkpoints/llamaX-rt-int4 \
  --baseline checkpoints/llamaX-fp16 \
  --prefix tests/longprefixes/chain50k.txt \
  --seed 42
```
observed: tokens identical until ~32768 then start diverging; kv-index check raises index_mismatch at that boundary. Logs:```
[2026-03-19T03:14:12Z] INFO kv: prefill_apply count=32768 shard=2
[2026-03-19T03:14:12Z] WARN rope: wrap_candidate pos=32768 period=40960
[2026-03-19T03:14:12Z] ERROR kv_check: expected_idx=32768 got_idx=65504 layer=18
```

lee: that ERROR pattern (expected==32768, got==65504) smells like a nibble-pair read where byte alignment is off by 8 bytes -> high/low nibble swapped across words. Did you inspect the serialized blob headers?

jana: yes, quick metadata diffs:```
- exporter.version: ref-2026.03
- exporter.roundtrip: true
- pack.alignment: 0 -> 8
- payload.offsets: 0, 16384, 32768 -> 8, 16392, 32776
```
so the roundtrip tool inserted an 8-byte padding before some layers (not all).

omar: why would it be inconsistent across layers? Maybe our merger aligns shard boundaries to 8 for some fragments. If kernels assume 16B alignment, an 8B shift will flip which nibbles are interpreted for int4 dequant loads. Over long contexts RoPE phase cycling amplifies the tiny error to token-level divergence.

ci-bot: quick check run: loader asserts alignment when LOADER_STRICT=true. The rt-int4 artifact failed with offsets at 8 mod 16.

jana: confirmed: running with LOADER_STRICT=1 triggers:```
AssertionError: layer 18 kv_buffer.offset % 16 == 0 -> 8
```

lee: options: 1) change serializer to preserve 16B alignment and avoid inserting padding; 2) make loaders copy-unpack to an aligned buffer if misaligned; 3) modify kernels to support unaligned reads (very invasive). My vote: (1) + (2) as fallback.

omar: agree. For short-term patch, copy-unpack in loader is quickest and safe. I can prototype a zero-copy fastpath when payload already aligned, otherwise memcpy into aligned mmap. Overhead: small (measured ~1.1s on 28GB file on dev server).

jana: perf cost sounds acceptable as stopgap. We should also add a regression in model-onboard to run longctx_compare with a 50k+ prefix for any roundtripped int4 assets. If it diverges vs fp16, reject onboarding.

lee: I'll open serializer PR to preserve packing/alignment semantics (ensures pack.alignment == 0). Also add unit that serializes -> reload -> bit-compare tensor bytes.

ci-bot: ci plan created: onboarding: add job `roundtrip-int4-longctx` with seeds [7,13,42] and prefix set sample50k.txt. Failure mode blocks merging of artifacts into the catalog.

perf-bot: scheduled nightly eval: rundir=rt-int4-fuzz, seeds=10, prefix=sample50k.txt, start=2026-03-19T23:00Z. Will report per-seed earliest divergence token.

jana: thanks — assigned tasks: omar -> loader memcpy PoC; lee -> serializer PR + unit test; jana -> update onboarding doc and wire CI job. I'll leave thread open until perf-bot posts results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
